symbols.name: _rewrite_by_window
symbols.note: Internal method for window-based rewrite; returns (content, reason) tuple.

symbols.name: _run_rewrite
symbols.note: Applies scoped write without tool loop; writes files and tracks backups.

claims.text: BOTTOM-UP. Splicing the last window first keeps every not-yet-applied window's line numbers valid even when a correction changes the line count above it.
claims.why: The code iterates over sorted windows in reverse order, splicing the last window first.

claims.text: The expected answer is the same fragment plus a tiny edit. Without an output cap Ollama may keep a malformed JSON string alive until the whole remaining context is exhausted; the first real 81-line window did exactly that for >7 minutes.
claims.why: The code computes output_cap and passes num_predict=output_cap to limit generation length.

claims.text: urllib's request is not cooperatively cancellable. Bound each generation so a stop/wall-clock request cannot be hidden behind the provider's 300 s default.
claims.why: The code sets timeout_s=min(float(timeout_s), 60.0) to cap generation time.

claims.text: Greenfield CREATE: a path that doesn't exist yet is a creation request, not an error -- the same guard gates it, the backup is None (rollback deletes it), and the quality checks that compare against the original are skipped because there is no original.
claims.why: The code sets creating = not target.exists() and later sets self._backups.setdefault(str(target), target.read_bytes() if target.exists() else None).

claims.text: WINDOWED path: the caller named the lines that are wrong, so the model is asked for those lines instead of a reprint. No hint (or an unusable one) falls through to the unchanged full-file behaviour below -- a window is never invented here.
claims.why: The code checks if windows is non-empty and calls _rewrite_by_window only if windows is truthy; otherwise falls through to full-file rewrite.

claims.text: Preserve the pre-window full-rewrite contract: text-mode reads expose universal newlines to the prompt and text-mode writes restore the platform convention.
claims.why: The code replaces \r\n and \r with \n for the prompt and later uses target.write_text(content, encoding='utf-8') for full rewrites.

claims.text: Shared baseline (daedalus.lanes): truncation, parses, content substitution, unresolved first-party imports -- in that order, cheapest and most specific refusal first. Substitution and imports are the two guards this lane was measured to be missing on 2026-07-30; they are not optional extras, they are baseline.
claims.why: The code calls run_checks with _CHECK_POLICY, but the implementation of run_checks and _CHECK_POLICY is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Backup None = created file (rollback deletes it). Track any parent dirs we create so rollback can prune them too (mirrors the tool loop).
claims.why: The code sets self._backups.setdefault(str(target), target.read_bytes() if target.exists() else None) and appends created parent dirs to self._created_dirs.

claims.text: Window splicing promises that bytes outside the measured fragment stay identical even when the checkout uses LF on Windows.
claims.why: The code writes windowed files using target.write_bytes(content.encode('utf-8')) instead of write_text, bypassing newline translation.
